title: How Worker Co-ops Work
summary: Josh and Chuck explain worker cooperatives ("co-ops"), tracing their roots from Robert Owen's Owenism and New Harmony, Indiana, through the Rochdale Pioneers in England, Black American cooperatives after the Civil War, farmer alliances, and the Knights of Labor. They cover the International Cooperative Alliance principles and how co-ops are governed, then survey large examples: Mondragon in Spain, the Kerala-based cooperative in India, Italy's government support, Argentina's recovered companies, Mexican fishing co-ops, the Cooperative Home Care Associates in the Bronx, Maximum Fun, Island Employee Cooperative in Maine, employee-owned Publix and ACE Hardware, and pros and cons. The episode ends with a listener mail about Ponti City Tower in Johannesburg.

segments.title: Opening banter and what worker co-ops are
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck introduce worker cooperatives, the co-op versus coop spelling, and the Sevenanda grocery in Atlanta as a familiar example, then contrast co-ops with the capitalist model of wage labor.

segments.title: Owenism and New Harmony
segments.summary: Robert Owen's Owenism, his 1825 experiment at New Harmony, Indiana, and its ties to socialist ideas and the way the word socialism is avoided in the US.

segments.title: Rochdale Pioneers
segments.summary: The 1844 Rochdale Pioneers in England, the flannel-weaving origins, the first cooperative store and its reinvention as a community project, and the later growth into the Cooperative Group.

segments.title: Black cooperatives after the Civil War and labor republicanism
segments.summary: Post-Civil War Black cooperatives, including the Colored Caulkers Trade Union Society in Baltimore led by Isaac Myers and the Colored Farmers National Alliance and Cooperative Society, plus the idea of labor republicanism.

segments.title: Knights of Labor, AFL and the International Cooperative Alliance
segments.summary: The Knights of Labor's co-op goals and their decline in favor of the American Federation of Labor, and the founding of the International Cooperative Alliance in 1895.

segments.title: Ad break
segments.summary: Sponsor break before the nuts and bolts section.

segments.title: How co-ops work: Rochdale Principles and governance
segments.summary: The Rochdale Principles adopted by the ICA in 1995: voluntary open membership, democratic one-member-one-vote versus share-based voting, capital controlled democratically, autonomy, education, cooperation among co-ops, and community service. Also probation periods, buy-in, and elected boards.

segments.title: Help for starting co-ops in the US
segments.summary: Resources in the United States such as the Northwest Cooperative Development Center and the Cooperative Fund of the Northeast for converting businesses or starting co-ops, and how the US support is less robust than in other countries.

segments.title: Mondragon, Spain
segments.summary: The Mondragon Corporation in Spain's Basque region, founded by priest José María Arizmendiarrieta, its origins in a 1956 kerosene heater co-op, its roughly 80,000 employees, its governance, the six-to-one pay ratio, and profit sharing and pay cuts in downturns.

segments.title: Kerala cooperative in India
segments.summary: A large road-contracting cooperative founded in Kerala in 1925 with about 18,000 employees, and the support of Prime Minister Nehru for co-ops in India.

segments.title: Italy, Argentina and Mexico
segments.summary: Italy's government support for co-ops and employee buyouts of failing firms, Argentina's National Movement of Recovered Companies in the early 2000s, and Mexican fishing co-ops that self-regulate sustainability.

segments.title: US co-ops: home care, Maximum Fun, Maine island stores
segments.summary: The Cooperative Home Care Associates in the Bronx, the largest US co-op, its member buy-in and social mission; Maximum Fun becoming a worker-owned co-op; and the Island Employee Cooperative of three Maine stores.

segments.title: Employee stock ownership, Publix, ACE Hardware
segments.summary: Employee stock ownership plans (ESOPs) distinguished from co-ops, Publix as the largest employee-owned US company, ACE Hardware's independent retailer model, and a note on ACE return policies.

segments.title: Pros and cons of co-ops
segments.summary: Co-op pros such as small pay gaps, low layoff rates, productivity, and long survival; cons such as slower decisions in a crisis. Also a shout-out to co-op platforms Subvert and Fair.

segments.title: Co-op job satisfaction and decision speed
segments.summary: Discussion of quiet quitting, decision-making speed in co-ops versus capitalist firms, and job satisfaction.

segments.title: Listener mail: Ponti City Tower
segments.summary: Listener Bobby writes about Ponti City Tower in Johannesburg, a 1975 luxury building that decayed into a vertical slum and has been used in sci-fi films.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Closing credits and iHeartRadio production note.
